## Overview On ROCm, a MiniMax-M3 decoder layer whose `qkv_proj` is MXFP8 (e.g. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, whose attention projections are 1x32 MXFP8) runs the fused add + Gemma RMSNorm, writes the normed bf16 rows, and then `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` reads them back and quantizes them with a separate `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` launch. This PR quantizes the normed row per 32-element block in the epilogue of the norm kernel and hands `qkv_proj` a `QuantizedActivation`, so each layer drops one launch and the bf16 round trip. The fp8 values and E8M0 scales are bitwise equal to norm -> `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`, so the model output does not change. ## Claims - Norm + activation quant: 1.41x-2.06x per call (hidden 6144, M = 1-4096, bf16, MI355X); norm + quant + `qkv_proj` GEMM: 1.07x-1.19x. - Bitwise equal fp8 values, scales and residual vs. norm -> `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`, for bf16 and fp16. - MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP4, decode: the separate activation quant for `qkv_proj` disappears in 59 of 60 layers (kernel trace), the norm kernel time is unchanged, and the removed launches are 1.9% of decode GPU kernel time. AgentX P90 interactivity is 1.018x at concurrency 1 and 1.017x-1.045x at concurrency 16 (two runs, order swapped); c4, c8 and c32 are within run-to-run noise; GSM8K unchanged within stderr. - No change for layers whose `qkv_proj` is not served by `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` with fp8 weights, under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, with LoRA on `qkv_proj`, or with mono decode. ## Validation **Unit tests** (`tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_amd_ops.py`, already run by the AMD kernels CI step): 81 passed on this branch (MI355X, main nightly image with this branch's Python tree), 81 passed + 1 skipped with this PR applied on #63232. `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py` and `tests/v1/determinism/test_mx_linear_batch_invariant.py` (the existing consumer tests of the changed kernel): 97 passed. New tests: - `test_gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8_bitwise_eq_unfused`: `torch.equal` against `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` -> `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` for values, scales and residual, n in {2048, 3072, 6144}, bf16 and fp16. Every row has a block with a scale above 1, an all-zero block and a tiny block (`1 + w = 2**-8`), plus all-zero, tiny, single-block-dominated and partly-zero rows. - `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_qkv_proj`: a real `QuarkOCP_MX` MXFP8 layer (per-row scales, 32x32 block scales, and K % 128 != 0, where the weight is dequantized to bf16 at load), M in {1, 37}. Checks the producer gate (fuses iff the kernel reads the fp8 activation as is) and that `qkv_proj(QuantizedActivation)` is bitwise equal to `qkv_proj(norm output)`. - `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_off_under_batch_invariance` **Microbenchmark** (method as in #59782: one HIP graph of 128 back-to-back calls cycling through 16 input sets, best of 5; MI355X; hidden 6144, bf16; `qkv_proj` is 2560 x 6144 at TP4). "separate" is `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` + `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` (current behaviour), "fused" is `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8`. Speedup of fused over separate: | M | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | 256 | 1024 | 4096 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | norm + quant | 1.66x | 1.58x | 1.58x | 1.57x | 1.58x | 1.59x | 1.64x | 1.70x | 2.06x | 1.41x | 1.49x | | norm + quant + qkv GEMM | 1.18x | 1.16x | 1.15x | 1.16x | 1.19x | 1.15x | 1.09x | 1.10x | 1.10x | 1.07x | 1.11x | The plain `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` (the kernel gains a `QUANT_MXFP8` constexpr) is unchanged: the separate path times within 1% of the pre-PR kernel at every M. **End to end**: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP4, MI355X, mono decode off, FULL_DECODE_ONLY CUDA graphs, on #63232 (`8d0f05a0c`, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash`) with this PR applied on top; baseline is the same image unchanged. AgentX trace replay (InferenceX), 600 s per point, `max-num-seqs` = 2 x concurrency, the arm that runs first alternates per concurrency. opt / baseline (> 1 is better): | Concurrency | P90 interactivity | |---:|---:| | 1 | 1.018x | | 4 | 0.990x | | 8 | 1.106x | | 16 | 1.017x | | 32 | 1.064x | GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, full test set of 1319, greedy, concurrency 16): baseline 96.51 / opt 96.44 strict-match (stderr 0.51 / 0.51), flexible-extract 96.44 / 96.36. The difference is one question; vLLM is not batch invariant at concurrency 16, so greedy outputs vary between runs even with bit-identical kernels. ## Details - **Producer and consumer.** `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` declares `kMxfp8Dynamic` as its input quant key and accepts a `QuantizedActivation` on the `dot_scaled` and block32 GEMMs; `QuarkOCP_MX` exposes the key for MXFP8 layers (ModelOpt MXFP8 already does). The `QuantizedActivation` contract itself is unchanged. - **Scale layout.** `kMxfp8Dynamic` does not encode the scale layout: the FlashInfer MXFP8 kernels read swizzled scales under the same key, this kernel reads row-major `[M, K // 32]`. So the producer (`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8`) also requires the consumer to be `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` with fp8 weights, the same way DeepSeek V4.1's `can_fuse_query_quant` checks for the FlashInfer kernels. If a `QuantizedActivation` reaches the kernel for a weight it dequantized to bf16 at load (K % 128 != 0), `apply_weights` dequantizes the activation instead of failing; the producer does not fuse in that case. - **Other producers of `kMxfp8Dynamic`.** On main, no other producer fuses into a Quark MXFP8 linear: DeepSeek V4.1's query-quant fusion is CUDA-only and requires the FlashInfer kernels, and `maybe_fused_act_quant` has no MXFP8 entry. ModelOpt MXFP8 MiniMax-M3 checkpoints on ROCm also take this path (same kernel, same bitwise result). - **First layer.** Layer 0 has no residual and uses the non-add `gemma_rmsnorm`; it keeps the separate quant (1/60 of the calls on M3.1-Flash). A non-add variant is a small follow-up if wanted. - **Batch invariance, LoRA.** Off under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, like the other producer-side quant fusions (#59069), so that mode keeps exactly the path `tests/v1/determinism` covers. With LoRA on `qkv_proj`, `get_input_quant_key` returns `None` and nothing changes. - **Mono decode.** The `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO` executor calls `input_layernorm` and `self_attn` directly, so it is unaffected; the end-to-end numbers are with mono off. - **No new env var.** The output is bitwise equal, so there is no accuracy reason to turn it off. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

#### 1. 🔵 Nit: Fusion decided pre-load from unprocessed layer state
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1386`

`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` runs in `MiniMaxM3DecoderLayer.__init__`, before `process_weights_after_loading`. Pre-load `weight_scale` is `[N, K//32]`, so the `weight_scale.shape[0] != weight.shape[0]` branch of `supports_quantized_input` is dead there and the decision reduces to `K % 128 == 0`. This is conservative and never fuses wrongly: both post-load fp8 paths (block32 and `dot_scaled`) consume the pre-quantized input when `K % 128 == 0`. The only effect is that fusion is skipped for 32x32 block-scale checkpoints with `K % 32 == 0` but `K % 128 != 0`, which `rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm` could serve. Consider noting the pre-load evaluation in a comment, or deciding after load.

**Who is affected:** Only hypothetical block-scaled MXFP8 checkpoints whose hidden size is a multiple of 32 but not 128 on gfx95x lose the fusion; the default MiniMax-M3 `hidden_size` of 6144 always fuses.

#### 2. 🔵 Nit: Model couples to concrete kernel class via attribute duck-typing
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1295`

`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` imports the concrete `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` and finds it by attribute name (`scheme.ocp_mx_linear` for Quark, `quant_method.kernel` for ModelOpt). If either attribute is renamed, the fused input-norm MXFP8 path turns off without warning; output stays correct and only the speedup is lost. The Quark path is covered by `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_qkv_proj`, which asserts the fusion is on for K % 128 == 0; the ModelOpt lookup is not tested. The class check is a documented workaround because `kMxfp8Dynamic` does not encode scale layout (row-major vs FlashInfer swizzled), already tracked as a TODO in `quant_activation.py`. A small accessor such as a kernel getter, or a layout field in the quant key, would remove the duck-typing.

**Who is affected:** MiniMax-M3 AMD users with MXFP8 (Quark/ModelOpt) checkpoints on gfx950, only if those attributes are later renamed; the result is a silent performance regression, not a correctness bug.

**Related past reviews:** [#50605](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50605) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/rocm_native.py`

#### 3. 🔵 Nit: Pre-quantized activation path skips scale shape/layout validation
`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/rocm_native.py:314`

The `QuantizedActivation` branch of `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel.apply_weights` passes `qa.scale` to `_mxfp8_dot_scaled_gemm` / `rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm` without checking its shape (`[M, K//32]`), dtype (uint8) or row count against `qa.data`. `kMxfp8Dynamic` does not encode scale layout, so a future producer handing in a mismatched 2-D scale would get wrong output rather than an error. No current producer can do this: the only one routed to this kernel is MiniMax-M3's fused norm, which checks the kernel type and writes contiguous row-major scales. The K alignment is already enforced by `supports_quantized_input`. Cheap defensive asserts would still help.

**Who is affected:** No current configuration; only a future producer that sends non-row-major `kMxfp8Dynamic` scales to the ROCm dot_scaled kernel.

#### 4. 🔵 Nit: Third inline copy of MXFP8 block quant math
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/gemma_rmsnorm.py:103`

The `QUANT_MXFP8` epilogue in `_gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_kernel` repeats the block-quant math of `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel`: the amax/`TINY` clamp, the `sb` formula, the [0,254] clamp and the `exp2(127 - sb)` reciprocal multiply. `_swiglu_oai_quant_kernel` already had a copy, so this is a third. The docstring's 'bit-identical to `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`' refers to the ROCm Triton path, which is what `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` dispatches to for these 2D row-major inputs. The new test checks this bitwise with `torch.equal`, so any future drift would fail the test. Consider factoring the block quant into a shared `@triton.jit` helper, or naming `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel` as the reference in the comment.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers changing the MXFP8 quant math on ROCm; there is no runtime impact today.

_Verified by running it._

**Related past reviews:** [#46117](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46117) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/rocm_native.py`

#### 5. 🔵 Nit: Forward fusion branch not exercised by any test
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1401`

No test drives the new fused branch in `MiniMaxM3DecoderLayer.forward`. `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_qkv_proj` builds the `QuantizedActivation` by hand and calls `scheme.apply_weights` directly. The end-to-end `amd_specialized_decode/test_model.py` excludes `self_attn` from Quark quantization, so `fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` is never True there. A regression in the residual handoff, `orig_shape`/dtype, or norm weight/eps in this hunk would go unnoticed. The hunk currently reads correctly; consider a small layer-level test, or quantizing `qkv_proj` in the mini model.

**Who is affected:** Only maintainers changing this code: it lacks regression coverage on gfx950 with an MXFP8-quantized `qkv_proj`; no runtime misbehavior was found.

_Verified by running it._

#### 6. 🔵 Nit: Module docstring stale after adding third entry point
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/gemma_rmsnorm.py:19`

The module docstring now lists three entry points (`gemma_rmsnorm`, `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm`, `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8`), but the next paragraph still says "Both normalize over the last dim ...". That wording is stale and should cover all three. The MXFP8 variant's flattened `[M, N]` output and `N % 32 == 0` requirement are already documented in its own docstring and enforced by an assert. At most, the module paragraph could point to that docstring.

**Who is affected:** Readers of `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/gemma_rmsnorm.py`; documentation only, no runtime effect.

_Verified by running it._

**Related past reviews:** [#9138](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/9138) on `csrc/layernorm_quant_kernels.cu`

#### 7. 🔵 Nit: Fusion skipped when residual is None; MTP log overstates
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1398`

The MXFP8 fused path only runs when `residual is not None`, and only `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8` has the MXFP8 epilogue. So the model's first decoder layer on the first PP rank and the MTP `transformer_layer` (called with `residual=None` in `mtp.py`) always run the unfused `input_layernorm` -> `qkv_proj` quant path. Non-first PP ranks receive `residual` from `intermediate_tensors`, so their first layer does fuse. `fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` is still computed as True for the MTP layer even though it can never take that branch. Consider a comment, or a non-residual `gemma_rmsnorm` MXFP8 variant.

**Who is affected:** MiniMax-M3 on ROCm with an MXFP8 `qkv_proj` using `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`: layer 0 on the first PP rank and the MTP draft layer keep the separate quant (performance only).

#### 8. 🔵 Nit: ModelOpt kernel fallback branch untested and likely unreachable
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1307`

The ModelOpt fallback in `_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` (reading `quant_method.kernel`) is reachable but untested. `ModelOptLinearMethod.create_weights` calls `expose_input_quant_key`, and on gfx95x `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` selects `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`, whose key is `kMxfp8Dynamic`. The new tests only build Quark layers (`_quark_mxfp8_linear`). Consider adding a ModelOpt MXFP8 `qkv_proj` case to `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_qkv_proj`.

**Who is affected:** ModelOpt MXFP8 MiniMax-M3 checkpoints on gfx95x ROCm, where the fusion decision for `qkv_proj` goes through the untested `quant_method.kernel` lookup.

_Verified by running it._

+def _mxfp8_edge_case_inputs(n: int, dtype: torch.dtype):
+    """(x, residual, weight) whose normed output covers the MXFP8 block cases.
+
+    Through the weight, every row gets a huge block (scale above 1.0), an
+    all-zero block, and a tiny block (``1 + w == 2**-8``). Rows: 32 ordinary
+    rows with a residual, then an all-zero row, a row of tiny values, a row
+    whose first block dwarfs the rest, and a row of partly-zero blocks.
+    """
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    w = torch.randn(n, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype) * 0.1
+    w[:32] = 300.0
+    w[32:64] = -1.0 + 2**-8
+    w[64:96] = -1.0
+
+    ordinary = torch.randn(32, n, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype)
+    zero = torch.zeros(1, n, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype)
+    tiny = torch.full((1, n), torch.finfo(dtype).tiny * 16, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype)
+    dominated = torch.randn(1, n, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype) * 1e-2
+    dominated[:, :32] = 1e4
+    partly_zero = torch.randn(1, n, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype)
+    partly_zero[:, ::2] = 0.0
+    partly_zero[:, 128:192] = 0.0
+    x = torch.cat([ordinary, zero, tiny, dominated, partly_zero])
+
+    res = torch.zeros_like(x)
+    res[:32] = torch.randn(32, n, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype)
+    return x, res, w
+

#### 1. 🔵 Nit: Fusion decided pre-load from unprocessed layer state
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1386`

`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` runs in `MiniMaxM3DecoderLayer.__init__`, before `process_weights_after_loading`. Pre-load `weight_scale` is `[N, K//32]`, so the `weight_scale.shape[0] != weight.shape[0]` branch of `supports_quantized_input` is dead there and the decision reduces to `K % 128 == 0`. This is conservative and never fuses wrongly: both post-load fp8 paths (block32 and `dot_scaled`) consume the pre-quantized input when `K % 128 == 0`. The only effect is that fusion is skipped for 32x32 block-scale checkpoints with `K % 32 == 0` but `K % 128 != 0`, which `rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm` could serve. Consider noting the pre-load evaluation in a comment, or deciding after load.

**Who is affected:** Only hypothetical block-scaled MXFP8 checkpoints whose hidden size is a multiple of 32 but not 128 on gfx95x lose the fusion; the default MiniMax-M3 `hidden_size` of 6144 always fuses.

#### 2. 🔵 Nit: Model couples to concrete kernel class via attribute duck-typing
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1295`

`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` imports the concrete `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` and finds it by attribute name (`scheme.ocp_mx_linear` for Quark, `quant_method.kernel` for ModelOpt). If either attribute is renamed, the fused input-norm MXFP8 path turns off without warning; output stays correct and only the speedup is lost. The Quark path is covered by `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_qkv_proj`, which asserts the fusion is on for K % 128 == 0; the ModelOpt lookup is not tested. The class check is a documented workaround because `kMxfp8Dynamic` does not encode scale layout (row-major vs FlashInfer swizzled), already tracked as a TODO in `quant_activation.py`. A small accessor such as a kernel getter, or a layout field in the quant key, would remove the duck-typing.

**Who is affected:** MiniMax-M3 AMD users with MXFP8 (Quark/ModelOpt) checkpoints on gfx950, only if those attributes are later renamed; the result is a silent performance regression, not a correctness bug.

**Related past reviews:** [#50605](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50605) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/rocm_native.py`

#### 3. 🔵 Nit: Pre-quantized activation path skips scale shape/layout validation
`vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/rocm_native.py:314`

The `QuantizedActivation` branch of `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel.apply_weights` passes `qa.scale` to `_mxfp8_dot_scaled_gemm` / `rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm` without checking its shape (`[M, K//32]`), dtype (uint8) or row count against `qa.data`. `kMxfp8Dynamic` does not encode scale layout, so a future producer handing in a mismatched 2-D scale would get wrong output rather than an error. No current producer can do this: the only one routed to this kernel is MiniMax-M3's fused norm, which checks the kernel type and writes contiguous row-major scales. The K alignment is already enforced by `supports_quantized_input`. Cheap defensive asserts would still help.

**Who is affected:** No current configuration; only a future producer that sends non-row-major `kMxfp8Dynamic` scales to the ROCm dot_scaled kernel.

#### 4. 🔵 Nit: Third inline copy of MXFP8 block quant math
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/gemma_rmsnorm.py:103`

The `QUANT_MXFP8` epilogue in `_gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_kernel` repeats the block-quant math of `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel`: the amax/`TINY` clamp, the `sb` formula, the [0,254] clamp and the `exp2(127 - sb)` reciprocal multiply. `_swiglu_oai_quant_kernel` already had a copy, so this is a third. The docstring's 'bit-identical to `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`' refers to the ROCm Triton path, which is what `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` dispatches to for these 2D row-major inputs. The new test checks this bitwise with `torch.equal`, so any future drift would fail the test. Consider factoring the block quant into a shared `@triton.jit` helper, or naming `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel` as the reference in the comment.

**Who is affected:** Maintainers changing the MXFP8 quant math on ROCm; there is no runtime impact today.

_Verified by running it._

**Related past reviews:** [#46117](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46117) on `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp8/rocm_native.py`

#### 5. 🔵 Nit: Forward fusion branch not exercised by any test
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1401`

No test drives the new fused branch in `MiniMaxM3DecoderLayer.forward`. `test_fused_input_norm_mxfp8_qkv_proj` builds the `QuantizedActivation` by hand and calls `scheme.apply_weights` directly. The end-to-end `amd_specialized_decode/test_model.py` excludes `self_attn` from Quark quantization, so `fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` is never True there. A regression in the residual handoff, `orig_shape`/dtype, or norm weight/eps in this hunk would go unnoticed. The hunk currently reads correctly; consider a small layer-level test, or quantizing `qkv_proj` in the mini model.

**Who is affected:** Only maintainers changing this code: it lacks regression coverage on gfx950 with an MXFP8-quantized `qkv_proj`; no runtime misbehavior was found.

_Verified by running it._

#### 6. 🔵 Nit: Module docstring stale after adding third entry point
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/gemma_rmsnorm.py:19`

The module docstring now lists three entry points (`gemma_rmsnorm`, `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm`, `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8`), but the next paragraph still says "Both normalize over the last dim ...". That wording is stale and should cover all three. The MXFP8 variant's flattened `[M, N]` output and `N % 32 == 0` requirement are already documented in its own docstring and enforced by an assert. At most, the module paragraph could point to that docstring.

**Who is affected:** Readers of `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/gemma_rmsnorm.py`; documentation only, no runtime effect.

_Verified by running it._

**Related past reviews:** [#9138](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/9138) on `csrc/layernorm_quant_kernels.cu`

#### 7. 🔵 Nit: Fusion skipped when residual is None; MTP log overstates
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1398`

The MXFP8 fused path only runs when `residual is not None`, and only `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp8` has the MXFP8 epilogue. So the model's first decoder layer on the first PP rank and the MTP `transformer_layer` (called with `residual=None` in `mtp.py`) always run the unfused `input_layernorm` -> `qkv_proj` quant path. Non-first PP ranks receive `residual` from `intermediate_tensors`, so their first layer does fuse. `fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` is still computed as True for the MTP layer even though it can never take that branch. Consider a comment, or a non-residual `gemma_rmsnorm` MXFP8 variant.

**Who is affected:** MiniMax-M3 on ROCm with an MXFP8 `qkv_proj` using `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`: layer 0 on the first PP rank and the MTP draft layer keep the separate quant (performance only).

#### 8. 🔵 Nit: ModelOpt kernel fallback branch untested and likely unreachable
`vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1307`

The ModelOpt fallback in `_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8` (reading `quant_method.kernel`) is reachable but untested. `ModelOptLinearMethod.create_weights` calls `expose_input_quant_key`, and on gfx95x `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel` selects `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`, whose key is `kMxfp8Dynamic`.
